key_insight: This paper shows that calibrating the individual experts in a mixture-of-experts model can improve both reliability and performance, especially when data distribution shifts. It clarifies when calibration actually helps MoE systems instead of just making probabilities look better.
problem_solved: It addresses the lack of understanding around when and why calibration improves mixture-of-experts models, particularly under distribution shift where model predictions can become unreliable.
method: Study calibration at the level of individual experts rather than only the final ensemble output.
Analyze mixture-of-experts behavior under distribution shift to identify conditions where calibration improves performance.
Compare predictive accuracy and uncertainty reliability to determine when calibrated experts lead to better MoE outcomes.
impact: For practitioners, this provides guidance on building MoE systems that remain trustworthy when deployed in changing real-world environments. It helps improve both confidence estimates and decision quality in applications where uncertainty matters.
visual_elements: A diagram of a mixture-of-experts pipeline showing expert outputs, gating, and calibration steps
Before-and-after reliability diagram comparing uncalibrated vs calibrated predictions
A distribution shift illustration showing training vs deployment data changes
An accuracy vs calibration trade-off chart for different MoE variants
paper_title: Toward Calibrated Mixture-of-Experts Under Distribution Shift
paper_authors: Gina Wong, Drew Prinster, Suchi Saria, Rama Chellappa, Anqi Liu
